western_alliance.aa_structure: multi-region national footprint evaluated under a Fed-approved CRA Strategic Plan; the Phoenix assessment area is one of several regional-division AAs and is the one targeted
western_alliance.ask_basis: anchored on the TARGET assessment area, and on the bank's OWN published goal for that assessment area rather than on inferred capacity. The 2024-2026 CRA Strategic Plan (Fed-hosted) sets a Phoenix assessment area donations goal of $465K-$695K/yr for satisfactory and $580K-$865K/yr for outstanding. Their 2023 actual in that assessment area was $466,412 — $1,412 above the satisfactory FLOOR and $113,588/yr short of the outstanding floor. A $25,000 grant closes 22% of that shortfall.
western_alliance.verify_note: Verified 2026-08-22 from the May 27, 2025 Federal Reserve public evaluation (published Aug 10, 2026 — the most recent PE in the roster). The PE states: 'The Phoenix assessment area consists of Maricopa and Pinal counties in their entirety.' Evaluated under a STRATEGIC PLAN, so there are no Lending/Investment/Service component ratings; performance is measured against five negotiated, published dollar-and-count goals. Goal Four is 'Dollar amount of donations made to qualified community development organizations' — a literal dollar target a grant to us counts toward.
western_alliance.pe_giving: $1.8 million in qualified donations in the Phoenix assessment area over the 2021-2023 plan period (Exhibit 13: $606,127 / $702,789 / $466,412; aggregate $1,775,328)
western_alliance.pe_need_quote: donations … helped to meet various community and credit needs in the assessment area, including … other community services to low- and moderate-income individuals and families
western_alliance.documented_gap: Sharpened against the successor plan. Phoenix CD donations fell 34% from $702,789 (2022) to $466,412 (2023). Under the 2024-2026 plan that run-rate sits $1,412 above the satisfactory interim floor of $465,000 and $113,588 below the outstanding interim floor of $580,000. The bank must add roughly $114K/yr in Phoenix donations to reach outstanding, and the goal escalates 5% in each of years two and three. Separately, Goal One (small business lending by dollar) was not met at the satisfactory threshold in Phoenix in the prior plan.
western_alliance.cluster_role: Maricopa anchor — the only large-institution CRA funder whose assessment area actually contains Maricopa County. Maricopa is the 4th largest SNAP enrollment gap in the country.
